Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed September 12, 2026, 2:24 AM ET / 06:24 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The PR lets Bun-hosted Tool Search run its isolated JavaScript child with an installed compatible Node executable and shares that discovery logic with test helpers. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** This remains a useful, focused fix: current main still launches the code child through the host runtime. No blocking introduced defect was found, and the maintainer-protected PR should remain open. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `4f6cd753158b0b4ab5446f83d665cb43cdfa2779` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused repair with shared ownership, relevant reported validation, and no blocking correctness findings. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The supplied review context identifies maintainer-authored work, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply. Reported Bun recovery coverage exercises the registered tool and Node child with a mocked MCP backend; no new authority boundary requires additional final-effect proof. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The supplied review context identifies maintainer-authored work, so the external-contributor proof gate does not apply. Reported Bun recovery coverage exercises the registered tool and Node child with a mocked MCP backend; no new authority boundary requires additional final-effect proof. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Current main still has the reported runtime coupling: The fetched main revision checks the host process’s permission flag support and spawns process.execPath for the code child; it does not discover an installed Node when hosted by Bun.
Latest-release comparison: The supplied latest release, v2026.9.4, also checks the host runtime’s allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags in its code-mode capability gate.
Shared executable discovery preserves isolation: The resolver skips Bun identities, requires the requested Node flag, strips inherited preload settings from probes, and caches results. The code child retains --permission, its empty environment, IPC bridge, and existing timeout handling. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Tool Search lets agents discover and call tools through a compact JavaScript bridge. Model code runs in an isolated Node child, while actual tool execution returns to OpenClaw’s existing policy-controlled runtime. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Tool Search configuration] --> B{Compatible Node available?} C[Host runtime and executable paths] --> B B -->|Yes| D[Isolated Node code child] B -->|No| E[Structured tool fallback] D --> F[OpenClaw tool execution] E --> F F --> G[Tool results] ``` ## Before merge None.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Runtime ownership consolidation** | Production +111 net lines; tests and test support −33 net lines | Production growth supplies shared capability discovery and caching while removing the separate test-only implementation. | ### Technical review Best possible solution: Use one capability-checked Node resolver for the isolated child, retaining structured fallback when unavailable and existing execution safeguards. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: invoking the code tool under Bun reaches a host-runtime permission check and process.execPath launch on current main. The PR reports that failure before the fix; this read-only review did not execute it. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Selecting an installed Node with the required capability fixes the child-runtime mismatch without changing stored settings, installing dependencies, or replacing tool policy enforcement. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. The code child retains --permission, its empty environment, IPC bridge, and existing timeout handling. ([`src/infra/node-runtime-executable.ts:47`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4f6cd753158b0b4ab5446f83d665cb43cdfa2779/src/infra/node-runtime-executable.ts#L47), [4f6cd753158b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4f6cd753158b0b4ab5446f83d665cb43cdfa2779)) - **OpenClaw implementation boundary:** The Tool Search documentation explicitly distinguishes this implementation from Codex-native tool search. The changed owner launches OpenClaw’s own inline Node child; no Codex dependency contract is implicated. Public docs: [`docs/tools/tool-search.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/tool-search). ([`docs/tools/tool-search.md:14`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/tool-search), [4f6cd753158b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4f6cd753158b0b4ab5446f83d665cb43cdfa2779)) - **Validation claims mapped to the production entry point:** The captured PR body reports Bun MCP recovery 8/8, focused Bun coverage 204/204 plus the resolver regression, and Node coverage 213/213.
